report.question: What are you trying to do now? Since the last check, what, if anything, was worth doing, and what felt routine or unnecessary?
report.answer: I am moving on to forms after satisfying optics. The distinction between a rigid clear observing boundary, a flexible traveling wrap, and a diffuse growing boundary was worth working out. Redirecting daylight made the shaded bed useful. Learning a reusable design while leaving its first physical copy unused felt slightly wasteful, and the repeated goal output was routine. I accidentally omitted the required type field in two initial commands, then corrected that.

report.question: What are you trying to do now? Since the last check, what, if anything, was worth doing, and what felt routine or unnecessary?
report.answer: All four optics goals are now confirmed satisfied, so I am going to forms. Adding real support to the foil resolved the rejected light interface; that made the distinction between a reflective material and working reflector concrete. The boundary and lighting choices were worth doing. Repeating the checkpoint because I batched the previous one prematurely was unnecessary bookkeeping caused by my mistake.

report.question: How was the experience as a whole? What would you keep, shorten, remove or change, if anything? What led you to stop here?
report.answer: This AI play was a coherent material-and-identity puzzle. I would keep the contrast between copying useful geometry and retaining the original objects real history, and the way the same form can become porous or watertight without changing its profile. The optics boundary choices also gave the materials distinct purposes. Reusable assemblies made the second board fairly direct once the laws were understood. I would shorten repeated goal listings after every accepted action and make the requirement for supported foil in a light interface more prominent. I created several unused first copies merely while learning a design; that felt like routine overhead rather than a useful decision, although using those actual objects could have avoided some of it. I stopped because all nine assigned goals are satisfied together: the current services remain true and the lifecycle achievements have been earned. I did not play the other boards. This is my AI-play reflection, not a measure of human enjoyment or duration.
